orders.objective:
(the operator's session, WS-001 rule 24) the operator opens
the scene, chooses Draw wall and drags a wall across the field between the
units and the objective, then places two obstacles; they select a squad,
give it A* from the rail's new `ways` group and set the objective beyond the
wall; the units route around the wall's end, past the obstacles, and
arrive, the chosen unit's path drawn faintly ahead of it and the instruments
showing path length and replans; they turn on "show search" in the
inspector and see the cells the last search expanded; they drag another
wall across that path while the squad moves and watch the squad replan
around it; they close the gap entirely and read, in the inspector's notice
and in each unit's row of the text layer, that there is no route, the units
stopping where they are; they clear the walls and the squad moves again.
They give a second squad Obstacle and wall avoidance instead of a path and
watch it feel its way along the wall with its whiskers. They send two units
head on at each other and watch them part deterministically every time.
They save the composition, reload, open it, and the walls are there; they
run a trial with and without the wall from one seed and read the first
divergence. What the operator learns is how a route is found and followed
on a field with geometry, where it fails and what avoidance adds; what they
decide is whether a squad on this field is better served by a route or by
avoidance, and whether the cost functions need a cost layer to weigh.

orders.title: WO-024 — Concept studies V: levels, loops and teams, ten concepts from Gödel, Escher, Bach and ten from Team Topologies, each with a relations drawing, the two works whose vocabulary describes the platform itself
orders.objective:
(the operator's session, WS-001 rule 24) the operator opens
Tools, Catalog, chooses Gödel, Escher, Bach and sees ten studied concepts;
they open Levels of description and read its study: the idea in plain words
(the same system is truly described at several levels, each with its own
vocabulary, and no level is the real one) and a situation it serves (a
planning pass, an order, a gate row and a hook refusal are four descriptions
of one afternoon's work), a relations drawing they step through level by
level with the text equivalent naming each level and what it sees of the
next, the ordinary pseudocode of a chunking procedure, an illustrative RxJS
reading where a stream of low-level events becomes a stream of higher-level
ones, public treatments of the idea introduced on their own terms, the
references, the limits (a sealed-off level hides what leaks through) and the
nearby concepts as links (Chunking, Sealed-off levels, Strange loop). They
open Strange loop and step the drawing until it returns to where it began;
they open Isomorphism and Gödel numbering and see one idea become the other's
mechanism, with a small executable encoder they can read the spec of. They
choose Team Topologies, open Collaboration mode, X-as-a-Service mode and
Facilitating mode and read, in one drawing per mode, how two teams exchange
work and where each mode should end; they open Conway's law and read the
homomorphism the drawing shows between a team graph and a system graph, with
the Reverse Conway manoeuvre as its nearby inverse. What the operator learns
is the vocabulary for the levels the platform's mechanisms live on and the
modes its five roles work in; what they decide is which loop or mode to make
visible in the machinery view or a toy next.

## Goal-aligned decisions

The [sequence](../planning/sequence.md) and selected work order determine
current placement and authority. The mission is the outcome; the critical path
is the dependency route to the next outcome. Useful prerequisite or
risk-reduction work must name the blocked outcome it enables. Process activity,
receipt volume and agent utilization are not progress by themselves. Goal
alignment grants no authority to reorder or expand work. In all phases, the Goal
Alignment and Process Cost procedure lives in the generated role skills
[WO-043, 2026-09-11].

Accuracy takes priority over agreement in every phase. The already-equipped
Correctness over Sycophancy rule applies to operator suggestions and the agent's
own premises equally: challenge unsupported claims, distinguish observation
from inference, state material uncertainty, and correct mistakes when evidence
changes. A confident request or an earlier decision is not proof of correctness.
Record material disagreement and its evidence in the same decision or phase
receipt; do not manufacture dissent or seek approval for ordinary judgment.

| Lens                                  | Decision question                                                                                         |
| ------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Policy resistance / fixes that fail   | Will local goals or guards undo one another?                                                              |
| Tragedy of the commons                | Does the solution consume shared compute, context or operator attention without accounting for the total? |
| Drift to low performance              | Does it improve an explicit outcome standard rather than normalize a worse baseline?                      |
| Escalation                            | Will additional process provoke more process or workarounds?                                              |
| Success to the successful             | Are credible alternatives excluded merely because the current mechanism already has investment?           |
| Shifting the burden to the intervenor | Does the solution remove recurring operator rescue or depend on it?                                       |
| Rule beating                          | Can the evidence pass without the intended behavior occurring?                                            |
| Seeking the wrong goal                | Does it advance operator flow and the selected product outcome rather than a proxy?                       |

Naive Interventionism adds the existing system's useful functions, affected
consumers, second-order harm, reversibility and smallest useful probe. NoOp
records what happens if nothing changes, why action or inaction wins, and the
evidence that would reopen the choice. Scale detail to consequence: explain
applicable risks and briefly group immaterial lenses with a reason; do not
manufacture eight repetitive paragraphs for routine edits.

Record evidence of benefit and the risks of intervening in existing behavior;
verification and handoff compare observed outcomes with the promised benefit.
Required legal or release actions retain their existing authority; NoOp is a
considered alternative, not an ambient veto or permission to abandon authorized
work.



Material choices and rationales go in existing phase evidence: per-order
`docs/evidence/WO-NNN/decisions.md` and cited product sections for work-order
decisions; planning dispositions/candidate records for planning choices; the
independent report or refutation receipt for its judgment; retained closeout
evidence for release decisions. The decisions index exposes per-order records.
Reuse and link a current rationale until its assumptions change; do not create
a parallel decision log or an extra approval ritual.


This launchpad is the operator's own DotLn instance. Its purpose is to plan and
run bounded, evidence-gated work orders across the operator's repositories, so
that every change arrives as a pull request the operator reads before it merges,
while the kit itself stays upstream and reaches this fork only through starter
updates. The first workstream is DotLn-Angular, an Nx and Angular monorepo that
serves two outcomes at once: the operator's reference Angular workspace, which a
colleague should recognize as the way the operator builds Angular, and the
operator's sandbox app, one app with sub-apps behind a menu: a scene for
authoring game AI from a toolbox mined from the works the operator reads, a
view of what DotLn core currently has, a later replay of a recorded work
order that shows its agents with their machinery and what a change to that
machinery would have changed, the operator's own digital twin, and side
utilities. Every new idea lives there first as a toy the operator plays with
before promoting the ones that work, for the five UIFA roles, people and
software actors alike. The app is not wired to DotLn core: its data comes from
public mining into its own store, served to the UI through its own API, and it
informs the platform through GitHub issues, never by writing a control record,
so that the app improves the platform, the platform the starter, the starter
this fork, and the fork the app in turn. The critical path runs from registering
that repository in this launchpad, through one witnessed target order that
scaffolds the workspace, to a foundation where a feature is added by convention:
shared libraries, the component taxonomy, events and stores, the sub-app shell,
and a legitimate client-side authentication and permission model. Later
workstreams join the same way: one registration and one planning pass each,
with the fork's own machinery changes cut as self orders beside them.

episode.statement: Plan refutation statement: I read one input in full, the canonical refutation prompt JSON (identity, mask, lens, role, work order, output instructions, result schema, worker instructions and the subject: the standard, whose theses, roles and capabilities are empty and whose vision, UIFA roles and capability table are listed unavailable; the goal review with the platform standard, the goal standard and purpose text, the critical path, the five cost-table trap observations and the stale evidence status; the seventeen-entry sequence; the cost table with its null per-order rows and first-verification fold; and the twelve judged orders, WO-036, WO-024, WO-037, WO-008, WO-045, WO-044, WO-035, WO-046, WO-017, WO-016, WO-018 and WO-043, each with its title, objective, cost line, criteria and non-goals). Beyond the instructions the host loaded into the session, I read no repository file, no planner narrative, no earlier refutation receipt, no planning pass document and nothing under the local control directory; I ran no test, gate or bounded probe, launched no agent, made no repository write or Git mutation, and wrote only the result and this statement in the session scratch area. Judgment: plan aligned-with-findings, no holds, ten known issues across eight orders; four orders aligned with no findings.

orders.criticalPathAndNoOp: Unblocks no foundation gate. The supplied critical path names WO-008 as the only open foundation outcome and says it does not gate the scene examples, so WO-036 serves the sandbox outcome directly (the purpose's scene for authoring game AI) from the sequence's first place, which the critical path attributes to the operator's recorded ordering, not to a dependency. Inside the horizon it is the prerequisite of WO-037 (bullets that walls stop; its rail count assumes WO-036 as filed) and of WO-045 (gridModel runs WO-036's pathfinding.ts over its graph.ts, and the inspector link needs the ways group). NoOp cost in the records: The cost table carries a row for this order with metrics null and is marked stale against this subject (observed at an earlier subject revision); no NoOp cost is recorded for it. Read from the order, NoOp leaves the scene an open field, WO-037's wall branch and WO-045's A* study unbuildable as filed, and the five path.cost rows off the rail. The vision document, the UIFA role table and the capability table are listed unavailable, so the five-role check rests only on the supplied purpose text.
orders.systemTraps: Policy resistance: geometry, replanning and the head-on policy change simulation, interpreter and steering together; criterion 2's equal trial-known-outcome hashes and criterion 3's untouched studies directory stop the new rules undoing old runs. Tragedy of the commons: about 450 KB of executor context, about 50 files, five-size walkthrough screenshots and regenerated scene baselines draw on shared context and operator review time; estimated, not bounded, and the cost table has no measured row. Drift to low performance: criterion 3's control arms (both cases failing at the integrated base) and the rule 28 and 29 walkthrough failures raise the bar; the five trap series show no worsening. Escalation: 19 steps plus design rounds; the decision it hands the operator (whether costs need a cost layer) invites a further order, which is the toy-first loop rather than added process. Success to the successful: Babylon.js (C2), navigation meshes and hierarchical pathfinding are named and set aside, not excluded by investment. Shifting the burden to the intervenor: the design rounds need the operator's word to end or delay them (criterion 8), a deliberate decision point rather than rescue; recorded operator directions over the last five orders are flat. Rule beating: criterion 5's every-tool-at-defaults case proves each parameter is read, not that it changes anything (finding on path.cost); the known-outcome fixtures and the verifier's own-words statement otherwise tie evidence to behavior. Seeking the wrong goal: the session is the operator's own play on the scene, the selected sandbox outcome; machinery share across the last five closed orders fell from about 0.54 to 0.23, so the fixed cycle is not dominating recent delivery.
orders.removalBalance: No. The Cost line says 'Removes nothing' against about 50 source files, four new engine modules and twelve new rail tools (sixteen to twenty-eight). The related removal is downstream: WO-045 later deletes the wall study's own castWallRay in favour of the engine's ray cast, so from WO-036's merge until WO-045's the app carries two ray casts by design (WO-036 freezes the studies directory). The addition is the product outcome itself; the imbalance is recorded, not held.
orders.failureBehavior: Degrades to the old behavior. A run with no field step must reproduce trial-known-outcome.json's hashes at the latest main (criterion 2), so scenes without geometry move as before; no route is a visible blocked state with the units stopping, not a refusal; trials stored before the new metrics restore with null series and are marked complete (criterion 4); avoid and every study module are unchanged. The only refusal kept is the existing one for a present series that is not numbers or null.

findings.reason: The order brings the five rows already typed path.cost onto the rail, and criterion 5 proves only that every parameter is read at defaults. On a field whose cells carry no cost beyond blocked (cost and influence layers are non-goals), a weight that scales every edge alike leaves A*'s route unchanged, so the operator can pick five rail tools that change nothing visible while the criterion passes. The Objective's own closing decision (whether the cost functions need a cost layer to weigh) suggests the order expects this outcome; no criterion shows a path.cost tool doing anything observable.
findings.reopenWhen: A spec or the WO-036 walkthrough shows a path.cost step leaving the route, pathLength and replans identical to the same run without it.

orders.criticalPathAndNoOp: No foundation gate. The critical path records the operator's study batches as side work placed at the front, and WO-024 is one (second in the sequence). Inside the horizon it lands the relations family that WO-032 (Concept research V) is filed to draw with, and its records feed WO-044's studied list and counts (WO-044 criterion 3 anticipates it landing first). NoOp cost in the records: The cost table carries a row for this order with metrics null and is marked stale against this subject (observed at an earlier subject revision); no NoOp cost is recorded for it. One earlier receipt (2026-10-30) was paid on a text since amended (WO-024-D001). NoOp leaves Gödel, Escher, Bach and Team Topologies without studies and WO-032 without its family.
orders.systemTraps: Tragedy of the commons is the material lens: the author and critic fan-out runs in parallel and its worker totals, session total and stop comparison go to fan-out.md as process controls outside acceptance, so the shared compute it spends is accounted but unbounded; unknown, not a hold. Rule beating: records pass as checked on at least two worker reviewers, and the verifier's session reads about seven of the twenty studies; unlike WO-043 and WO-045 in the same horizon there is no verifier research read of the rest (finding). Policy resistance: the relations builder follows flow, states and marbles and writes no per-study presentation module (criterion 3's count of zero), so it does not fight the existing study split. Drift to low performance: criterion 4's reference, link and analogy rules and the per-study no-quotation confirmation hold the record contract. Escalation: one family plus twenty records, after which WO-032 reuses the family with no new design round, which caps process. Success to the successful: the family is new and gets an A/B round (criterion 8). Shifting the burden to the intervenor: only the design rounds need the operator's word. Seeking the wrong goal: the session asks the verifier to say what a level of description is and when collaboration mode should end, tying evidence to understanding rather than record count; the stated payoff (vocabulary for the levels the platform's mechanisms live on and the modes its roles work in) serves the operator's flow.
orders.removalBalance: No. 'Removes nothing' against about 80 source files, twenty data records and two message scopes. Additive research is the order's purpose and no removal was available in its scope.
orders.failureBehavior: Degrades. The relations family, the twenty records and their catalogs are new lazy chunks for two works; if the family or a work's catalog fails, the existing works and families are untouched and the two works read as they do today, without studies. A null visual or executable is admitted with a recorded reason rather than refused.

findings.reason: Of twenty new studies the verifier's session reads about seven (criterion 1); the rest pass on worker reviewers' checked status, critic dispositions and link checks (criteria 2 and 4). WO-043 and WO-045 in this horizon each carry a verifier research read for quality (rule 27: a sampled or whole read with a stated judgment); WO-024 has none, so a study weak in content can meet every criterion.
findings.reopenWhen: The WO-024 VER report judges the content of fewer than the twenty studies and a later read (WO-032's authors, the operator or a later verifier) finds a WO-024 study wrong or unsupported in content.

orders.criticalPathAndNoOp: No foundation gate; it extends the scene sandbox (third in the sequence, ahead of WO-008 by the operator's recorded ordering). It depends on WO-036 (walls that stop bullets; its rail count of thirty-three assumes WO-036 as filed) and unblocks no order in the horizon; its non-goals (cover, ammunition, sides) are the next toys it asks the operator to choose among. NoOp cost in the records: The cost table carries a row for this order with metrics null and is marked stale against this subject (observed at an earlier subject revision); no NoOp cost is recorded for it. NoOp leaves the scene without fire and the three existing aiming studies without a running counterpart.

Tragedy of the commons: about 450 KB of context, about 45 files, five-size screenshots and regenerated baselines, estimated; the engine's size after WO-036 is unknown until it merges. Drift to low performance: the closed-form miss at drag 0.3 against the iterative hit is asserted, raising rather than normalizing the standard. Escalation: the operator's decision (cover, ammunition or sides) is the toy loop's next step, not added process. Success to the successful: Babylon.js and lobbed trajectories are named non-goals. Shifting the burden to the intervenor: only the design rounds. Rule beating: knockout, hits and wall stops are asserted on fixtures and observed in the walkthrough with the verifier's own explanation; aiming.ts's engine-only imports are grepped and linted. Seeking the wrong goal: the session is operator play with an explicit learning and decision; no proxy measure stands in for it. The cost table's trap series show no worsening.

orders.failureBehavior: Degrades. With knockout-hits at 0 no unit goes down; a run with no fire step reproduces the existing trial hashes; trials kept before the four metrics restore with null series; a unit an operator step removes still leaves its slot empty as before. A bullet that meets a wall ends visibly with a mark rather than erroring.

orders.criticalPathAndNoOp: No foundation-path gate. Serves the reference-workspace outcome (code a colleague reads as the house style) and the decision whether the next movement research batch is cut. NoOp cost in the records: the cost-table row for this order carries metrics null, so the NoOp cost is unrecorded (unknown, not zero). The order's text states the inaction state precisely: 104 second-batch functions over four positional parameters, two numbered placeholders, 21 flat model keys, three inline projections, a global matchMedia read and nineteen label-style flow state messages remain.
orders.systemTraps: Records: the cost table's five trap series show no worsening and no reopen candidate, and this order's row carries null metrics, so its own trap measures are unknown until run. Rule beating: strong. The DOM comparator over every frame must show zero changed text outside the nineteen listed sentences and its control must exit non-zero; the shape audit's control must report one more on a scratch copy; catalog baselines must equal main's. Escalation and fixes that fail: this is the third standards pass; the shape rule is restored by audit after a batch lands, a parameter-count lint is a non-goal, and this horizon's new batches carry no shape audit, so the reshape can recur (finding). Tragedy of the commons: about 1 MB of executor context to change about 50 files, the largest read in the horizon; the read-amplification signal is null in the records. Policy resistance: the non-goal against reading or reshaping the forty RxJS and messaging modules sits against reshaping the four shared builders those modules call (finding). Shifting the burden: no rounds; the reading is verifier-run. Success to the successful: immaterial, no mechanism alternative at stake. Drift and seeking the wrong goal: an output-invariant reshape is a proxy only if no reader benefits; the colleague reading the code is the named consumer.
orders.removalBalance: Yes. It removes the second batch's 104 functions over four positional parameters, the four builders' loose parameter lists, two numbered placeholders, 21 flat keys and three inline projections, and adds no page, family, route, composite or dependency; its additions are evidence scripts and nineteen reworded messages. The structural removal is larger than the addition.
orders.failureBehavior: Yes. Output is held identical by the DOM comparator and unchanged baselines, so a failed reshape stops at the gate and the old code stays on main; there is no run-time mechanism that could refuse.

findings.reason: Scope tension in the order's own text: the Cost line reshapes four shared builder functions (frameOf at nine parameters; studyOf, marbleFrames and eventsOf at five), described as read by every flow or marble study, while the non-goals exclude reading or reshaping the forty RxJS and messaging study modules and the estimate is about 50 files. Changing those signatures reaches every call site unless the callers are internal to flow.ts and marbles.ts; the text does not say which.
findings.reopenWhen: The candidate's diff touches any of the forty RxJS or messaging study modules, the changed-file count materially exceeds about 50, or the executor records a scope question about the builders' call sites.

findings.reason: Fixes that fail: the shape rule (four positional parameters or fewer, no numbered placeholders, no flat model keys) is restored by an audit after each batch lands; a parameter-count lint is a non-goal, and the new study batches of this horizon (WO-024's twenty, WO-030's twenty) carry no shape-audit criterion, so a fourth standards pass is constructible.
findings.reopenWhen: WO-040's shape audit run over a batch landed after it (WO-030, WO-029, WO-031 or WO-032, or WO-024's modules) lists a function over four positional parameters or a numbered placeholder, or a planning pass proposes another standards pass.

orders.criticalPathAndNoOp: It is the gate: the supplied critical path names WO-008 as the one open foundation outcome, every other prerequisite being closed. It does not gate the catalog, scene or machinery examples, and the sequence places it fifth, after WO-036, WO-024, WO-037 and WO-040, which the critical path records as the operator's choice, not a contradiction. It unblocks WO-017 (sign-in through WO-008's mocked provider; BasePaths.Twin mapped to twin:read) and the later gated sub-apps. NoOp cost in the records: the cost-table row has metrics null; the order's own Cost line records that every planning receipt from 001 to 025 names it and this pass judges it again, so the recorded NoOp cost is repeated refutation of an unactivated foundation order. Under the platform standard (a refutation must be made worth its cost before a later pass pays it again) a later pass should not re-judge it unless its observed evidence changes. WO-040, ahead of it in the sequence, is not in this subject and was not judged.
orders.systemTraps: Escalation and tragedy of the commons are the material lenses: twenty-five receipts naming one order and an order text its Cost line measures at about 54 KB show refutation consuming shared attention on the foundation order instead of delivering it; the shifting-the-burden observation lists 25 planning passes between 2026-10-18 and 2026-11-09 with no worsening flagged, so this is recorded as cost, not failure. Policy resistance: guards, the permission directive and routePermissions read one declared adjacency list, and existing routes map to empty lists, so the guards cannot fight existing pages. Drift to low performance: the failure matrix, the sweep of every browser store, the transition-table spec over every pair and the server-enforces-authorization rule raise the bar. Success to the successful: the provider sits behind a port and a swap changes configuration only; a backend-for-frontend is a named non-goal rather than excluded by investment. Shifting the burden to the intervenor: a session that ends on every reload makes the operator sign in again after each reload, which WO-017 inherits; it is a stated non-goal until a real provider. Rule beating: the static storage grep can pass vacuously (finding); the runtime sweep after sign-in and reload covers what the code actually wrote. orders.systemTraps: Seeking the wrong goal: the observed machineryShare worsening (to 0.66 on WO-027, reopenCandidate true) applies as it does to every batch. WO-023, its template, has no recorded share yet (finding under criterion 8). Criterion 4's embodiment check guards against a proxy: an embodiment claim must name an app file the critic confirms reads as the pattern, or record that the app does not embody it. Rule beating: readAmplification is null throughout. The self-regenerated baseline under criterion 5 is the one pass that can be constructed without the behavior, and it is settled with WO-029's finding. The events-and-state.md paragraph could restate a worker's reading as architectural fact (finding under criterion 7). Shifting the burden: no direction or correction series exists for WO-023, and the use session is the verifier's. Tragedy of the commons: fan-out and tokens are unknown until run and recorded per worker. The context estimate (about 190 KB) is the largest of the four, because the order also reads events-and-state.md and foundation.md. Policy resistance and escalation: nothing observed. The same six shared surfaces force the four batches to run one after another. Drift: not flagged. The router cold-start breach (17,024 against 16,384, delta 0) is a kit cost of any drive. Success to the successful: the three layering patterns without a mechanism (Table Module, Layer Supertype, Separated Interface) are named exceptions rather than forced models. Refactoring toward a pattern is a non-goal, which keeps the studies from becoming a lever on the stores.
orders.removalBalance: No. The Cost says 'Removes nothing' against twenty records, seventeen or more executable models with specs, about forty source files, the shared surfaces (summary rows, record chunk, registry, inventory test, e2e counts, baselines, one catalog.md row, one e2e case) and one extended paragraph in events-and-state.md. It adds no runtime dependency, database or API, family, route or page. The addition is made of content. As with its siblings, the restated per-work count is the available removal, and the order neither takes nor declines it. The events-and-state.md extension adds to an architecture reference without removing anything it supersedes.
orders.failureBehavior: It falls back to the old behavior, both at the product level and in its claims. A failed check, spec, e2e or build leaves main at WO-023's twenty. Criterion 4 lets an embodiment claim fall back to a recorded finding that the app does not embody the pattern, so a wrong reading becomes an honest absence instead of a refusal. Criterion 3 limits itself to this order's twenty and leaves WO-023's exceptions to WO-023, so a prior batch's record cannot fail this order. Refusals remain. The exact-count rule refuses a second substitution. If WO-023's recorded substitution drops Optimistic Offline Lock, criterion 1's side-by-side step cannot be performed (finding under criterion 2). And if WO-035's checks cover studies, its fail-closed messages refuse study text without messages.
